key_risk: ERCOT 2027 forward power prices are the whole argument and they are the thing that has fallen. Second, the money is getting expensive: the 09-14 424B2 prices $1.5B of junior subordinated notes at 7.000% and 7.250% to 2057, junior to about $18.3B of existing senior debt, to refinance preferred resetting in October and December 2026. Answered, and it is the reason the thesis works rather than an objection to it: a price that does not support new construction is a price that stops new supply from being built, which is exactly the condition under which an existing paid-for nuclear and gas fleet gets scarce as datacenter load arrives. The second objection — that the merchant complex is broken — is answered by separating VST from CEG: VST analyst revisions are improving (bullish share 91.7%, +0.4) while CEG deteriorates (82.1%, -3.1), and over the past month VST returned +1.32% against XLU at -7.11%, leading a sector being sold. Third objection, that the September filings signal distress, is answered by reading them: they are debt refinancing preferred, not equity, so there is no dilution.

thesis: J.B. Hunt lost 13.3% on 2026-09-16 after guiding Q3 down 5-10% from Q2, and the de-rating is larger than the news. Q2 was $1.91, so the guided range is about $1.72-1.81 against $1.76 actual in Q3-25 — the company described a roughly flat year-over-year quarter and the market removed 13.7%. It has beaten consensus in each of the last four quarters (+7.88%, +1.36%, +2.73%, +17.79%), and the CFO explained that JBHT recovers fuel through surcharges that lag, so it eats the cost until the fees catch up. Crude has now fallen four sessions to $95.59, and that lag runs in reverse on the way down: surcharges priced off higher fuel keep collecting while the fuel actually burned costs less.
key_risk: The fuel-lag argument only reaches part of the problem. Of the warning, $25M was additional driver expense — recruiting, training and signing bonuses — against $10M or more from fuel. Driver cost reflects a tight labour market, it is structural, and it will still be there when diesel is cheap. Worse, diesel may not actually get cheap: crude fell but distillate cracks are at all-time records with inventories 14% below the five-year seasonal average and refineries at 97.2% utilisation, so retail diesel at $6.05/gal can stay at a record even as crude falls. Insider flow is unhelpful — 0 open-market buys against 7 sells, -$4.74M over six months — and the stock lags SPY by 15.38% over one month and IYT by 6.52%.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that a cost warning from a bellwether is the first one, not the last, and that trucking is early-cycle exposed to a freight recession that has not finished — JBHT dragged the whole group down on 09-16 precisely because the market read it as an industry signal rather than a company one. Answered partially and honestly: the four-session base at 230.36-236.80 with closes clustered at 234-237 says the selling exhausted at a level rather than continuing, and the guided range being roughly flat year over year means the bar for Q3 is now low enough that the 4-for-4 beat record has something to beat. It is answered partially because the driver-cost line genuinely is an industry condition and this idea does not pretend otherwise — which is why it is sized at 2.5% and carries a 2.11 ATR stop rather than a tight one.

thesis: Five separate CarMax insiders bought stock in the open market inside four days in June — Barr 9,400 at $53.01, Bensen 2,500 at $52.20, ONeil 4,800 at $52.36, Chawla 2,000 at $53.39, Shinder 574 at $52.01 — for $1.27M with not one sale in the six-month window. A board-level cluster that tight is not personal liquidity management. The street has since capitulated in the same direction: the bullish share jumped 20.9 points to 28.0% as the book went from seven sell ratings and one strong sell in July to a single sell in September, while the company beat by 32%, 47% and 35% in its last three quarters.
key_risk: This is a levered consumer-credit business being bought at a moment when US10Y sits at 5.01%, and used-vehicle affordability is precisely what breaks when financing costs stay high — a de-rating that is 11.4% off the high but still 64.5% above the 200-session low has plenty of room to give back. The entry level is also unlikely to print unless something goes wrong: 52.00-54.50 is 7-10% below spot, so the most probable path to a fill is a disappointing 09-29 report, which is exactly why the order is explicitly cancelled rather than filled in that case. Expect this idea to simply not trigger.
counter_argument: The strongest case against waiting is that the insiders are already 9% up, the revision swing is underway, and a limit 7% below market on a name in an uptrend above its 200-day at 47.44 is an order that never fills — the classic dead pullback entry the strategy config warns about, which filled only 42% of the time in this report first month. That is conceded: this idea will probably not trigger, and it is captured anyway because the alternative is buying at 57.86 where an honest 2.0 ATR stop forces a target above the 200-session high. The floor is there to reject exactly this trade at this price, and the disciplined answer to a good thesis at a bad level is to name the good level, not to move the stop.
